Using Panoptes in a HADES package

Source: vignettes/using-panoptes.Rmd
using-panoptes.Rmd

This guide takes a HADES package maintainer from an ordinary package test suite to one package-owned behavior test that runs against every database platform the package declares. The examples use a fictional package named MyHadesPackage, begin with PostgreSQL, and then expand to the complete live database matrix.

1. Understand the ownership boundary

Panoptes owns reusable test infrastructure:

  • locating and validating the platform declaration;
  • selecting one DBMS per R process;
  • resolving normalized environment variables;
  • constructing DatabaseConnector connection details;
  • checking runner and operating-system compatibility;
  • managing temporary credentials and scoped SqlRender options;
  • generating collision-resistant database object names;
  • proving that a live connection was attempted; and
  • detecting drift between the declaration and the CI matrix.

The consuming package continues to own:

  • the list of databases it supports;
  • access to existing database servers and OMOP CDMs;
  • package-specific fixtures, behavior, and assertions;
  • database objects created by the test and their cleanup; and
  • GitHub environments, secrets, approvals, and trusted-run policy.

Panoptes does not provision a database or CDM and does not certify support by opening a connection alone. A green job must exercise meaningful package behavior and assert its result.

2. Add Panoptes as a test dependency

Add Panoptes to Suggests in the consuming package’s DESCRIPTION:

Suggests:
    Panoptes (>= 0.2.0),
    testthat (>= 3.0.0)

Panoptes belongs in Suggests, not Imports, because the package uses it only from tests and CI. This guide assumes Panoptes is available from its released repository, so consumers do not need a development Remotes entry.

3. Declare the supported platforms

Create the configuration directory and copy Panoptes’s installed template:

dir.create("inst/test-config", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
file.copy(
  system.file(
    "templates",
    "hades-database-platforms.yml",
    package = "Panoptes"
  ),
  "inst/test-config/hades-database-platforms.yml"
)

For a PostgreSQL-first adoption, reduce the copied file to a declaration like this:

schemaVersion: 1
package: MyHadesPackage
databaseConnection: subset
platforms:
  - dbms: postgresql
    enabled: true
    required: true
    cdmVersion: "5.4"
    connectionMode: server
    credentialMode: password
    tempEmulationSchema: false
    runner: ubuntu-latest
    os: any
    githubEnvironment: test-postgresql

The declaration is executable policy rather than a place to store secrets:

Field Meaning
databaseConnection none, subset, or all; all requires entries for every Panoptes adapter
enabled Whether the package currently claims and tests support for the platform
required Whether incomplete or incompatible explicit live CI must fail instead of skip
cdmVersion Default OMOP CDM version for the behavior test
connectionMode local, server, or connectionString
credentialMode none, password, or keyFile
tempEmulationSchema Whether Panoptes scopes SqlRender temporary-table emulation to the work schema
runner GitHub Actions runner used by the platform’s matrix row
os any, linux, windows, or macos compatibility requirement
githubEnvironment Protected GitHub environment supplying that row’s secrets

Use databaseConnection: subset and retain only platforms the package supports. Use databaseConnection: all only when all ten adapter entries remain in the file. A disabled entry must set required: false and provide a non-empty reason.

SQLite and DuckDB are local file-based platforms. Their entries must use connectionMode: local and credentialMode: none; HADES_DB_SERVER is the path to the database file. A consumer that runs DuckDB tests should also list the duckdb R package in Suggests. Neither local platform needs a JDBC driver.

Never put users, passwords, servers, connection strings, key contents, or schema values in this file. It is committed to source control.

Validate the declaration before writing the behavior test:

config <- Panoptes::readDatabaseTestConfig(
  path = "inst/test-config/hades-database-platforms.yml"
)
Panoptes::validateDatabaseTestConfig(config, package = "MyHadesPackage")

Unknown fields, duplicate DBMS entries, invalid field combinations, and missing required fields fail immediately.

4. Add a consumer integration test

Add tests/testthat/test-panoptes-integration.R. This test proves that Panoptes can discover the installed declaration and that the consumer declares the intended platforms:

Panoptes::skipIfLiveDatabaseTest()

testthat::test_that("Panoptes finds the package declaration", {
  config <- Panoptes::readDatabaseTestConfig(package = "MyHadesPackage")

  testthat::expect_equal(config$package, "MyHadesPackage")
  testthat::expect_equal(config$databaseConnection, "subset")
  testthat::expect_equal(
    vapply(config$platforms, `[[`, character(1), "dbms"),
    "postgresql"
  )
})

Do not copy Panoptes’s configuration, adapter, environment, or lifecycle unit tests into the consumer. The consumer integration test covers the boundary; Panoptes’s own suite covers the generic implementation.

5. Write one package-owned behavior test

Add a focused file such as tests/testthat/test-database-platform.R. The same test body should run for every selected DBMS. Keep DBMS branches out of the assertions; platform-specific connection behavior belongs in Panoptes.

testthat::test_that("package behavior works on the selected database", {
  testthat::skip_on_cran()

  config <- Panoptes::readDatabaseTestConfig(package = "MyHadesPackage")
  Panoptes::skipIfNoLiveDatabase(config)

  Panoptes::withDatabaseTestContext(config, verify = TRUE, {
    resultTable <- context$objectPrefix

    on.exit(
      MyHadesPackage::dropTestResults(
        connectionDetails = context$connectionDetails,
        workDatabaseSchema = context$workDatabaseSchema,
        resultTable = resultTable
      ),
      add = TRUE
    )

    result <- MyHadesPackage::runDatabaseBehavior(
      connectionDetails = context$connectionDetails,
      cdmDatabaseSchema = context$cdmDatabaseSchema,
      vocabularyDatabaseSchema = context$vocabularyDatabaseSchema,
      workDatabaseSchema = context$workDatabaseSchema,
      resultTable = resultTable
    )

    testthat::expect_true(result$succeeded)
    testthat::expect_gt(result$rowCount, 0)
    Panoptes::requireDatabaseTestConnectionAttempted(context)
  })
})

Replace the fictional runDatabaseBehavior() and dropTestResults() calls with the package’s real behavior and idempotent cleanup. Register cleanup before the behavior begins, and make it tolerate a partially created object. Use context$objectPrefix directly as an object name; Panoptes has already bounded it for DBMS identifier limits.

verify = TRUE opens and closes a connection before evaluating the test body. That proves reachability but does not replace the package assertions. requireDatabaseTestConnectionAttempted() prevents a required CI path from finishing green after an early return that never attempted a connection.

The context exposes these consumer-facing fields:

Field Consumer use
dbms Canonical selected DBMS name
connectionDetails Redacted-on-print DatabaseConnector connection details
cdmDatabaseSchema OMOP CDM schema
vocabularyDatabaseSchema Vocabulary schema, defaulting to the CDM schema
workDatabaseSchema Writable schema for package-owned test objects
cdmVersion Environment override or declared CDM version
tempEmulationSchema Work schema when temporary-table emulation is enabled, otherwise NULL
objectPrefix Collision-resistant, DBMS-bounded object name
platform Validated declaration entry for the selected DBMS

Panoptes removes temporary BigQuery key files and restores scoped options when withDatabaseTestContext() exits, including after an error. It never deletes objects created by the consumer test.

Optional focused live-test mode

The bundled workflow runs R CMD check with HADES_DATABASE_TEST=true. If the consumer wants that check to focus exclusively on the live behavior test, put this at the beginning of ordinary test files:

Panoptes::skipIfLiveDatabaseTest()

Do not add the guard to the live behavior test. This focusing mechanism is optional; omit it if the live job should also run the ordinary suite.

6. Run PostgreSQL locally

Download the matching JDBC driver explicitly. Panoptes constructs connection details but intentionally performs no network downloads:

$env:DATABASECONNECTOR_JAR_FOLDER = "$env:USERPROFILE\.jdbcDrivers"
driverFolder <- Sys.getenv("DATABASECONNECTOR_JAR_FOLDER")
dir.create(driverFolder, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
DatabaseConnector::downloadJdbcDrivers(
  dbms = "postgresql",
  pathToDriver = driverFolder
)

Set the normalized environment in the same PowerShell process:

$env:HADES_TEST_DBMS = "postgresql"
$env:HADES_DATABASE_TEST = "false"
$env:HADES_DB_USER = "..."
$env:HADES_DB_PASSWORD = "..."
$env:HADES_DB_SERVER = "server/database"
$env:HADES_CDM_SCHEMA = "cdm"
$env:HADES_WORK_SCHEMA = "scratch"
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "database-platform", reporter = "summary")'

HADES_DATABASE_TEST=false gives local-development behavior: missing values or an incompatible OS produce a test skip rather than a required-CI failure. A disabled or undeclared selection is a configuration error, and a real connection or behavior failure still fails the test.

HADES_VOCABULARY_SCHEMA defaults to HADES_CDM_SCHEMA, and HADES_CDM_VERSION defaults to the declared cdmVersion. Set either variable only when the environment differs. Panoptes print methods show variable names and set/unset status, never credential values or complete connection strings.

For a local DuckDB run, install the duckdb R package, select duckdb, and set HADES_DB_SERVER to an existing DuckDB file containing the test CDM. Keep the schema variables shown above, but omit the user, password, JDBC-folder, and driver-download steps. Panoptes opens the file through DatabaseConnector; it does not create or populate the CDM.

7. Provision GitHub environments and secrets

Create one protected GitHub environment for each enabled external platform. The environment name must match githubEnvironment, for example test-postgresql. Use the same normalized secret names in every environment; each adapter reads only the values its connection mode requires.

SQLite and DuckDB are local platforms and do not require protected GitHub environments or rows in the external-database matrix.

Connection style Required normalized secrets
Server and password HADES_DB_USER, HADES_DB_PASSWORD, HADES_DB_SERVER, HADES_CDM_SCHEMA, HADES_WORK_SCHEMA
Connection string and password HADES_DB_USER, HADES_DB_PASSWORD, HADES_DB_CONNECTION_STRING, HADES_CDM_SCHEMA, HADES_WORK_SCHEMA
Connection string and key file HADES_DB_CONNECTION_STRING, HADES_DB_KEY_FILE, HADES_CDM_SCHEMA, HADES_WORK_SCHEMA

For BigQuery, HADES_DB_KEY_FILE may be an existing file path or the key JSON contents. When it contains JSON, Panoptes writes a restricted temporary file and removes it on exit. The connection string must contain <keyfile path> where the generated path should be substituted.

Optionally define HADES_VOCABULARY_SCHEMA and HADES_CDM_VERSION. Do not create blank placeholder secrets; an unset optional value allows the documented default to apply.

Apply organization-approved reviewers and deployment rules to each environment. Pull requests from forks do not receive protected secrets. The bundled workflow skips fork-originated pull requests; a maintainer can evaluate trusted code with manual dispatch after it is present in the repository.

8. Configure live database CI

Copy the installed workflow template instead of maintaining a second full YAML example from this vignette:

dir.create(".github/workflows", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
file.copy(
  system.file(
    "templates",
    "database-platform-tests.yml",
    package = "Panoptes"
  ),
  ".github/workflows/database-platform-tests.yml"
)

For the PostgreSQL-first declaration, retain only the PostgreSQL matrix row. Whenever a platform becomes enabled in the declaration, add its DBMS, runner, and GitHub environment row in the same change. Packages declaring all adapters should retain all eight external rows from the template; SQLite and DuckDB remain local platforms and are not part of the live matrix.

The template provides:

  • pull_request and workflow_dispatch triggers, with no scheduled trigger;
  • one isolated job for each enabled external DBMS;
  • a safe condition that prevents fork pull requests from receiving live jobs;
  • the runner and protected environment declared for each matrix row;
  • normalized secret-to-environment-variable mapping;
  • cross-platform Java setup;
  • an explicit per-DBMS JDBC driver download;
  • declaration/workflow drift validation; and
  • R CMD check with HADES_DATABASE_TEST=true, focused on the live behavior test when the optional ordinary-test guards are present.

Panoptes does not define or require scheduled database testing. Trigger policy belongs to the consumer workflow.

9. Validate and roll out

Validate the static workflow locally whenever the declaration or matrix changes:

config <- Panoptes::readDatabaseTestConfig(
  path = "inst/test-config/hades-database-platforms.yml"
)
Panoptes::validateDatabaseTestWorkflow(
  config,
  ".github/workflows/database-platform-tests.yml"
)

The validator reports missing platforms, extra platforms, wrong runners, and wrong GitHub environment names. It expects exactly one row for every enabled external platform.

Begin with the PostgreSQL subset and run it using workflow_dispatch. After the package behavior and cleanup succeed, add the remaining supported platforms to the declaration and workflow together. A required matrix job must not be considered complete until it has used valid credentials, verified a connection, run the package assertions, and cleaned its objects.

Use these failure modes when diagnosing a job:

Symptom Meaning
Local test skips and names missing variables Complete the local environment or intentionally leave the platform unavailable
Required live CI reports missing variables The selected GitHub environment lacks required normalized secrets
Incompatible-platform error The workflow runner does not satisfy the declaration’s os policy
Driver or Java error Java or the selected JDBC driver was not provisioned before the test
Connection error Connection details were constructed, but the live verification failed
No-connection-attempt error Required CI exited before verification or meaningful behavior began
Cleanup error or leftover objects The consumer’s idempotent on.exit() cleanup is incomplete
Workflow-drift error The declaration and static matrix rows no longer agree

Maintenance checklist

When database support changes:

  1. update the declaration and workflow row together;
  2. provision or remove the matching protected GitHub environment;
  3. verify runner, OS, Java, and driver compatibility;
  4. update the declared CDM version or environment override intentionally;
  5. keep the behavior assertions equivalent across DBMSs;
  6. verify success and error paths both clean package-owned objects;
  7. run the consumer integration test and workflow validator; and
  8. run every required external platform before claiming support.
